audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 fits 48.76% over 804 games: Cassiopeia out-trades him at every level except 6, where a point-and-click suppression on a champion with no dash and no boots is a clean kill.
audit.corrected: Rating kept. The level-6 row is now the one row that says Malzahar, which is what makes the lane even rather than favoured.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer read Skill on rows 0-4 and 6 with Cassiopeia only on row 5, while the content layer read Skill/Cassiopeia/Cassiopeia/Cassiopeia/Malzahar/Cassiopeia/Cassiopeia and matched the packet levelChart. Six rows disagreed across layers, including level 6, where one layer said 'even' and the other said Malzahar kills you.
audit.why: The content chart is the one the kit supports. Malefic Visions at 650 and Call of the Void at 900 do not beat a poison-into-Twin-Fang stream at levels 2-5, and Nether Grasp at 6 unambiguously does.
audit.corrected: Moved phases[1], [2], [3] and [6] to Cassiopeia and phases[4] to Malzahar, rewriting the why on each so the sentence argues for the side it now sits on. win[N] already holds all of these values on disk, so there is no paired content edit to write — before would equal after — and after this the seven rows agree across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanics were described wrongly. Call of the Void was called a root in two content fields ('threatens a landed root', 'dodge his skillshot root') — Riot's text says it silences. Void Shift was called a 'passive shield' in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t — Riot's text says massive damage reduction and crowd-control immunity that lingers briefly after he takes damage. Neither is a shield and neither is a root.
audit.why: The difference is actionable in opposite directions. A silence means your escape is gone, not your movement — you can still walk out of the portal line. And because Void Shift is CC immunity rather than a shield, Petrifying Gaze does not land on a full-passive Malzahar at all; you have to chip him first.
audit.corrected: Corrected all of them, and added the two interactions the page never had: Nether Grasp is a channel that any crowd control on him breaks, and Malefic Visions passes to a nearby enemy if its target dies while afflicted.

audit.why: Nether Grasp's cooldown is the whole reason level 6 is survivable at all — 140 seconds at rank 1 is a very long punish window.
audit.corrected: Nether Grasp 140/110/80, Call of the Void 6s flat, Malefic Visions 11s at rank 1 and 650 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint). dosFull[2] told the reader to ground his retreat path; Malzahar has no dash, blink or movement ability, so the grounding half of Miasma does nothing here.
audit.why: Grounding advice against a champion with nothing to ground reads as a mechanic and is not one.
audit.corrected: Retitled that bullet to the Miasma slow, which is what actually holds him in the poison, and rewrote both bled bodies to their titles.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is close to even — Malzahar's Malefic Visions passive chips your HP through minions and Call of the Void threatens a landed root, but he has no way to all-in you yet without ult. Once you hit level 3 and can weave E into your Q-poison rotation, you start out-trading him in extended exchanges since he has zero mobility to escape your DoT once it's ticking. By level 5 you should be comfortably ahead in the trade math as long as you respect Void's range.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is close to even — Malefic Visions chips you through minions and spreads to a new target whenever its host dies, and Call of the Void threatens a silence, but he has no all-in without ult. Once you hit level 3 and can weave E into your Q-poison rotation, you start out-trading him in extended exchanges since he has zero mobility to escape your DoT once it's ticking. By level 5 you should be comfortably ahead in the trade math as long as you respect Void's 900 range.

notes: Two mechanics on this page were wrong, not just templated. Call of the Void silences; it was described as a root in two places. Void Shift is damage reduction plus crowd-control immunity; it was described as a 'passive shield' in three places, which matters because Petrifying Gaze does not land at all through CC immunity — you have to chip the passive off first, and that is now stated in dosFull[0].d. report[5].t still repeats the 'passive shield' wording; I left the report array alone per the two-entry cap, so that one line still needs correcting and is listed in unverified. I did not write anything about whether Petrifying Gaze specifically can break Nether Grasp once the suppression is already on you — suppression's interaction with your own casts is not in the kit file. The Miasma grounding advice in breakdown.mid ('ground every gank') and report[10].t ('ground Malzahar's escape') is inert against a champion with no movement ability; I fixed the bullets I rewrote and reported the rest.
